newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Tuesday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to easier but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from Monday's yield of 2.83/2.78 percent but one-year closed at a yield of 2.67/2.62 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.68/2.63 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$98.53/98.63.
May 2002 ended at S$99.53/99.58 against Monday's close of S$99.42/99.52 and June 2003 at S$94.57/94.62 versus S$94.43/94.53.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-5/8 2-1/2 percent from Monday's 2-1/2 2-3/8 percent.
